inputs.userGoal: Deploy primary and DR application stacks without Azure Front Door. Route the shared HTTP hostname novabank.dedroog.net to the West Europe primary and North Europe DR Web Apps through priority-based Azure Traffic Manager.
subGoals: Deploy production DR alongside primary in a separate novabank-prod-dr resource group.
Bind novabank.dedroog.net to both regional Web Apps without TLS.
Use Azure Traffic Manager priority routing with HTTP health probes.
Keep development inexpensive and ignore deploymentMode=dr.

reasoning.whyChosen: Separate resource groups allow primary, DR, and dev resources with immutable regional properties to coexist.
alternativesConsidered: Same resource group with suffixed resources
reasoning.tradeoffs: Additional resource groups add lifecycle boundaries but simplify regional failover operations.

resources.name: mode-derived virtual network and private DNS

reasoning.whyChosen: Each independently deployable environment needs regional delegated subnets and PostgreSQL private DNS.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Repeated address spaces prevent direct peering without renumbering, but the environments are not peered by this scaffold.

resources.name: mode-derived PostgreSQL Flexible Server

properties.drImplementation: Native Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers resource because AVM 0.16.1 does not forward sourceServerResourceId or pointInTimeUTC for GeoRestore

reasoning.whyChosen: Production primary creates geo-redundant backups; production DR restores them into Azure's paired North Europe region; dev uses the least expensive VNet-capable Burstable SKU.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Geo-restore has nonzero RPO/RTO and must use a distinct target server name. Production uses same-zone HA because West Europe cannot provision the requested geo-zone-redundant backup combination. Dev omits HA and geo backup.

dependencies: mode-derived virtual network and private DNS

resources.name: mode-derived App Service

properties.access: Production HTTP custom hostname and default App Service hostname; development HTTPS-only default hostname
properties.customHostnameDeployment: Two phase: deploy apps with binding disabled, publish asuid TXT and Traffic Manager CNAME records, then redeploy with binding enabled

reasoning.whyChosen: The same custom hostname can be bound to the two App Service apps because they are in different regions.
reasoning.tradeoffs: HTTP avoids certificate setup for the demo but does not encrypt application traffic. Production uses one non-zone-redundant P0v3 instance in each region.

dependencies: mode-derived virtual network and private DNS

reasoning.whyChosen: Traffic Manager provides DNS-based automatic failover while allowing the same custom hostname on apps in different regions.
reasoning.tradeoffs: DNS failover depends on resolver caching and does not proxy or encrypt traffic.

references.title: Configure Traffic Manager for an App Service domain

properties.implementation: Native Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces resource because the AVM does not expose dataAuthorizationMode

reasoning.whyChosen: Each environment keeps diagnostics in its own regional workspace, and DataActionsOnly ensures that control-plane roles do not implicitly grant log-query access.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Separate workspaces require cross-workspace queries for a global operational view. Subscription Owners cannot query logs directly but can still change RBAC or workspace configuration.

overallReasoning.summary: The subscription template derives location, resource group, resource names, SKUs, and PostgreSQL create mode from deploymentMode and environmentMode. Production adds a shared priority-based Traffic Manager profile and HTTP custom hostname.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Geo-restore is a disaster-recovery operation rather than continuous replication. Traffic Manager failover is DNS-based, and the demo custom hostname is intentionally unencrypted.

plan.validation: Dev ignores deploymentMode=dr; production primary and DR use separate resource groups and names; North Europe is the West Europe paired region; both production apps bind novabank.dedroog.net; Traffic Manager routes to primary with priority 1 and DR with priority 2; and Azure Front Door is absent.
